name: Low Carb Steak Fajita Skillet
writer_notes: SOURCE YIELD 4, rebuilt to 14 at the mapper's 3.5x scale. Every gram and buy string transcribed from mapped\low-carb-steak-fajita-skillet.json; no number computed in prose.

MACROS transcribed from the mapper's food-DB recompute at 14 servings, which EXCLUDES the two optional toppings: 540.9 cal, 56.5 g protein, 7.0 g carbs, 30.0 g fat per serving, reported as stat 541 / 57 / 7 / 30 and re-verified by build-v2-spec's food-macros-db recompute. In band for this run (400 to 650 cal, 35 g carb or less): 541 cal PASS, 7.0 g carbs PASS with a lot of room. Intro says 'under 10 grams of carbs', a true tighter bound at 7.0.

OPTIONAL TOPPINGS LEFT OUT OF THE COSTED BUILD ON PURPOSE. The source lists guacamole and sour cream 'for topping' as optional lines and serves it with low carb tortilla chips. The mapper's band macros exclude both toppings, and guacamole has NO commodity id (bid null) and NO food-macros-db row, so booking it would break the macro recompute and price a cost floor. So the 14-serving build is the nine core ingredients only. Guacamole and sour cream are noted in shop_smart as an optional day-of finish the shopper can grab separately, never as a booked ingredient and never as a make_it step, so the recipe cooks complete exactly as shopped. Tortilla chips are a serving suggestion, not an ingredient, and are not mentioned.

EVERY BOUGHT INGREDIENT IS USED BY A STEP and no step uses anything unbought. Walked the costed list against the steps both directions: beef (make_it 2 season, 4 sear, 5 finish, 6 combine), fajita seasoning (2), butter (3 saute + 4 sear, divided), red bell pepper (3), green bell peppers (3), yellow bell pepper (3), red onion (3), garlic (3), Mexican cheese blend (7). Nothing else is named in a step.

COST IS A FLOOR - FLAG FOR THE REPAIR PASS (map-owner domain, NOT edited here). db\ingredients.json has NO item row for 'Yellow Bell Pepper' and the 'bell-peppers' bid the mapper assigned it has no item row at all, so this build emits no bid for the yellow pepper and it prices pantry-static. This is the SAME known BID-MAP BLOCKER hatch-green-chile-chicken-casserole hit in this run. The yellow pepper (161 g, about 1.75 peppers) is therefore absent from the priced lines and cost_ps is understated by roughly that much, on the order of a dime a serving. The other eight bids all resolve on the live feed (butter, red-bell-pepper, green-bell-pepper, red-onion, garlic, sirloin-steak, fajita-seasoning, shredded-cheese). Fix is a map row for Yellow Bell Pepper -> bell-peppers at the map-owner stage, not here; no id minted, no price invented.

STEAK bid via the ingredient-map's Beef Flank/Sirloin Steak -> sirloin-steak entry plus the in-run flank-steak-parmesan precedent (mapper ruled_substitutions). The source line is 'skirt or flank steak' anchored by an explicit 2 lb weight; grams and printed weight agree by construction at 7 lb = 3175 g. Buy string says flank or sirloin so the shopper picks the cheaper of the same price class.

SHOP_SMART makes NO per-ounce, leftover, or lasts-several-batches claim, so no bullet needs a cost_lines entry to prove it. Every statement is grounded in the recipe's own buy amount, with package sizes referenced generically and never with a per-line cost. Cheese is named as the shredded Mexican blend to match the commodity the engine actually buys (shredded-cheese), so there is no block-beats-tub trap. Re-walk the bullets against cost_lines once costed before publish.

PORTION METHOD is the house weigh-the-pot: weigh the empty skillet in Step 1, weigh it full at the end, subtract, divide by 14. The whole batch cooks down in one skillet so the single-pot weigh is honest here.
intro_html: Fajitas are one of those dinners that already eat low carb if you just walk past the tortillas, and once you do that the plate gets a whole lot leaner without giving up a single thing you actually came for. This is skirt or flank steak sliced thin, seasoned hard, and seared fast, then folded back together with peppers and red onion cooked just to the point of tender. A blanket of melted cheese goes over the top and that is the meal. No wrap, no filler, just steak and vegetables doing the work. Built at 14 servings it lands around {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. That is a Tex-Mex dinner that loves your macros back.

Batch total: about $68.91 across 14 servings, so roughly $4.92 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $73.98 across 14 servings, roughly $5.28 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving at everyday prices for a steak fajita dinner you can eat all week, cheese and all. The steak carries the plate and the peppers stretch it, and nobody misses the tortilla.
shop_smart: Seven pounds of skirt or flank steak is the anchor. This is where most of the money and all of the protein live, so buy one big cut and slice it thin yourself instead of paying extra for pre-cut fajita strips. Flank and sirloin cook and slice the same way and sit in the same price class, so grab whichever one is cheaper the week you shop. Slicing goes easier if you firm the steak in the freezer for about twenty minutes first.

Three bell peppers and a red onion bring the color and the fajita flavor. One red, one green, and one yellow pepper plus a large red onion, all sliced into strips. Any mix of colors works if your store is short one, and the onion cooks down sweet against the peppers. These are cheap produce you can always find a use for.

Fajita seasoning and a little garlic do the seasoning. A couple of seasoning packets or a scoop from a jar coat all seven pounds of steak, and a few cloves of garlic go into the vegetables. That is the whole spice bill, and both are pantry backbone you already reach for.

A bag of shredded Mexican cheese blend finishes it. Three and a half cups melted over the top of the skillet is what turns steak and peppers into fajitas. Buy it pre-shredded in the blend so you are not grating three kinds of cheese by hand.

The classic toppings are optional and up to you. The original serves this with a spoon of guacamole and sour cream, and a few low carb tortilla chips on the side. None of that is in the fourteen-serving build or the cost below, so add whichever you like on the day you eat it and leave the rest off. The skillet is a full meal on its own.
make_it: Weigh your biggest skillet empty and write the number down. At the end you will weigh it full and subtract, which is the only honest way to split a batch this size into fourteen even servings.
Slice the steak thin against the grain and toss it with the fajita seasoning until every piece is coated. Let it sit while you get the vegetables going so the seasoning has a minute to grab.

Melt about half the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced red, green, and yellow peppers, the red onion, and the garlic, and saute just until the vegetables are tender but still have some bite, about four to five minutes. Scrape them onto a plate and set aside.

Melt the rest of the butter in the same skillet and turn the heat up high. Lay in the seasoned steak and sear it hard on both sides to build color, working in batches if the pan is crowded, because crowded meat steams instead of searing.
Turn the heat down to medium low and keep cooking the steak until it is no longer pink through. Pour any resting juices back in as you go.

Stir the peppers and onion back into the skillet with the steak and cook everything together for another minute so the flavors meet. Weigh the full skillet, subtract the empty weight from Step 1, and divide by 14 to find your serving weight.

Pull the skillet off the heat and blanket the top with the shredded cheese. Set a lid over it and let it stand about five minutes until the cheese melts, then portion that exact weight into each of your fourteen containers.
portion_html: The honest way to make fourteen even servings is by weight. Weigh the loaded skillet before the cheese goes on, subtract the empty weight you noted in Step 1, and that is your cooked total. Divide it by 14 and give each container that exact amount, then split the cheese evenly over the tops. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Weigh the empty skillet and note the number for portioning later.
Slice the steak thin against the grain and toss it with the fajita seasoning.
Saute the peppers, red onion, and garlic in half the butter until just tender, then set aside.
Sear the seasoned steak hard in the rest of the butter, then cook it through over lower heat.
Stir the vegetables back in, weigh the skillet, and divide by 14.
Top with the shredded cheese, cover to melt, and portion into fourteen containers.
